lines.native:
Sono Marginalia. Questa è la storia di Journathan, l'uomo dalle molte lingue. Il suo viaggio verso casa dura vent'anni.
I sell books only to people who understand them. No spoilers; it's about the journey, not the destination. Journathan hates that.
Dove va Journathan?
lines.translation:
I am Marginalia. This is the story of Journathan, the man of many tongues. His journey home lasts twenty years.
I sell books only to people who understand them. No spoilers; it's about the journey, not the destination. Journathan hates that.
Where is Journathan going?
lines.narrative: At The Old Bookshop, a bookworm emerges from a neatly eaten dictionary. She pencils a question mark beside your name.

lines.native: Un libro? No. È una cosa, non un luogo. Your reading comprehension remains in the prologue. Rileggiamo: «Il suo viaggio verso casa dura vent'anni.» Dove va Journathan?
lines.translation: A book? No. It is a thing, not a place. Your reading comprehension remains in the prologue. Let's reread: “His journey home lasts twenty years.” Where is Journathan going?
lines.narrative: Marginalia pencils a small correction in the air beside you. Apparently, you now have margins.

lines.native: Hai capito, ma la risposta è in inglese. The meaning is right; the language is on the wrong shelf. Reading comprehension: promising, technically unpublished. Rispondi in italiano: dove va Journathan?
lines.translation: You understood, but the answer is in English. The meaning is right; the language is on the wrong shelf. Reading comprehension: promising, technically unpublished. Answer in Italian: where is Journathan going?
lines.narrative: Marginalia pencils a small correction in the air beside you. Apparently, customers also have margins.

lines.native:
Esatto, a casa! Reading comprehension: officially out of the prologue. Ora leggo: «Il Ciclope chiede il suo nome. Journathan risponde: «Il mio nome è Nessuno.»»
The first recorded translation trick. Scholars wrote footnotes; the Cyclops had a difficult evening. Quale nome dà Journathan al Ciclope?
lines.translation:
Correct, home! Reading comprehension: officially out of the prologue. Now I read: “The Cyclops asks his name. Journathan replies: ‘My name is Nobody.’”
The first recorded translation trick. Scholars wrote footnotes; the Cyclops had a difficult evening. What name does Journathan give the Cyclops?
lines.narrative: Marginalia ticks the margin beside your name. The pencil mark looks provisionally charitable. She turns to a page she has only partly eaten.

lines.native:
Journathan è il suo vero nome. Ma quale nome dà al Ciclope? Leggi ancora: «Il Ciclope chiede il suo nome. Journathan risponde: «Il mio nome è Nessuno.»»
Correct man, wrong name tag. Reading comprehension: a footnote needs attention.
lines.translation:
Journathan is his real name. But what name does he give the Cyclops? Read again: “The Cyclops asks his name. Journathan replies: ‘My name is Nobody.’”
Correct man, wrong name tag. Reading comprehension: a footnote needs attention.
lines.narrative: Marginalia pencils a small correction in the air beside you. Apparently, customers also have margins.

lines.native: Esatto! Il nome è Nessuno. Hai capito il testo. Ora puoi comprare il libro. Reading comprehension: approved. Le pagine mancanti? La mia recensione era molto positiva.
lines.translation: Exactly! The name is Nobody. You understood the text. Now you can buy the book. Reading comprehension: approved. The missing pages? My review was very positive.
lines.narrative: Marginalia places a bookmark beside the passage. It has teeth marks, but so does the receipt.
